section_summary: This section comprises diplomatic and interdepartmental correspondence between the Japanese Embassy in Washington, the Department of State, and the Treasury Department from January to April 1939 regarding Federal income tax exemptions for Japanese government officials and non-diplomatic personnel stationed in or departing from the United States. Under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1938 and the Internal Revenue Code, the State Department certified reciprocal tax-exempt treatment by Japan for U.S. personnel, enabling Treasury to grant income tax exemptions and sailing permits to Japanese railway officials, naval and military inspectors, exposition delegates, language officers, and visiting scholars. The section concludes with the transmission and departmental scrutiny of a comprehensive roster of 36 non-diplomatic Japanese officials resident in the United States, including an internal inquiry concerning the official status of the Formosan Government Commissioner.

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests income tax exemption for Yasumichi Tasaka, the incoming resident representative of the Japanese Government Railways in New York City.
subfiles.summary: In Note No. 11, the Japanese Ambassador requests that Yasumichi Tasaka be added to the list of officials of the Japanese Government Railways in New York City granted exemption from taxation on their official salaries. Tasaka arrived in New York on January 12, 1939, aboard the steamship Tatsuta Maru to succeed Y. Yagami as resident representative.
subfiles.title: Note No. 11 from the Japanese Embassy to the Secretary of State Requesting Tax Exemption for Yasumichi Tasaka

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State transmits the tax exemption request for Yasumichi Tasaka to the Secretary of the Treasury with statutory certification of reciprocity.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits a copy of Japanese Embassy Note No. 11 concerning Yasumichi Tasaka of the Japanese Government Railways to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr. In accordance with Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1938, Hull certifies that Japan grants equivalent exemptions to U.S. government employees in Japan and that the character of the services performed is similar. Hull expresses the hope that Tasaka will be exempted from Federal income tax and that internal revenue officials will be advised accordingly.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury Regarding Tax Exemption for Yasumichi Tasaka
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury (Henry Morgenthau, Jr.)

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of the tax exemption request for Yasumichi Tasaka and reports its transmission to Treasury.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy Note No. 11 of January 24, 1939, regarding the desired income tax exemption for Yasumichi Tasaka. The note states that a copy of the communication has been transmitted to the appropriate authority of the United States Government to effect the tax exemption on his official compensation.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Acknowledging Note No. 11 Regarding Yasumichi Tasaka

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department acknowledges State's letter regarding the tax exemption of Minoru Yagami prior to his departure from the United States.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (John W. Hanes)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John W. Hanes acknowledges receipt of State's letter of January 21, 1939, regarding Minoru Yagami, Secretary of the Japanese Government Railways in New York, who intends to depart on February 4 aboard the steamship Aquitania. Hanes states that the matter is under immediate consideration in the Bureau of Internal Revenue and that State will be advised as soon as practicable.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Minoru Yagami

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms that Japanese naval officers attached to the Naval Inspector's Office in New York are exempt from Federal income tax.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (John W. Hanes)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John W. Hanes responds to the State Department's letter of January 6, 1939, enclosing Japanese Despatch No. 240 and a supplemental list of Japanese government employees. In view of State's certification under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1938, Treasury holds that the individuals named in the list are exempt from Federal income taxation on their official compensation. Appropriate instructions will be issued to the collectors of internal revenue for the relevant districts.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Exemption of Japanese Naval Officers

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State informs the Japanese Ambassador that Treasury has approved income tax exemption for the Japanese naval officers in New York.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State refers to Japanese Embassy Note No. 240 of December 23, 1938, requesting tax exemption for naval officers attached to the Naval Inspector's Office of the Imperial Japanese Navy Department in New York City. The Japanese Ambassador is advised that Treasury holds the officers exempt from Federal income taxation and that instructions will be sent to the collectors of internal revenue where they are stationed.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Regarding Tax Exemption for Naval Officers

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department rules that Tatsuo Shiraki of the Japanese Government Railways in New York is exempt from Federal income tax.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (John W. Hanes)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John W. Hanes references State's letter of December 22, 1938, concerning Tatsuo Shiraki, mechanical engineer and resident representative of the Japanese Government Railways in New York succeeding K. Yamanouchi. Pursuant to State's certification under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1938, Treasury holds that Shiraki is exempt from Federal income tax on his official compensation. Instructions will be issued to the Collector of Internal Revenue at the Customhouse in New York.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Tatsuo Shiraki

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests tax exemption and sailing facilitation for Masao Ogawa, Secretary to the Japanese Financial Commission.
subfiles.summary: In Note No. 17, the Japanese Ambassador states that Masao Ogawa, Secretary to the Japanese Financial Commission in New York since January 1937, will depart for London aboard the Aquitania on February 4, 1939. His salary being derived solely from the Japanese Government, the Ambassador requests that steps be taken to exempt Ogawa from income taxes and permit him to leave the United States without difficulty.
subfiles.title: Note No. 17 from the Japanese Embassy to the Secretary of State Regarding Masao Ogawa

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State transmits the tax exemption request for Masao Ogawa to Treasury with certification under Section 116(h).
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull writes to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr., referring to a telephone message to the Bureau of Internal Revenue regarding Masao Ogawa. Enclosing Embassy Note No. 17, Hull certifies under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1938 that Japan grants equivalent exemptions and that Ogawa's services are similar to those of American officials abroad. Hull requests that the Treasury Department instruct internal revenue officials to grant the exemption.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury Regarding Masao Ogawa
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury (Henry Morgenthau, Jr.)

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State confirms that telegraphic instructions were sent to exempt Masao Ogawa from income taxes upon departure.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges Note No. 17 of February 1, 1939, regarding Masao Ogawa of the Japanese Financial Commission. Confirmation is made of a telephone message stating that the Bureau of Internal Revenue would telegraph instructions to the Collector of Internal Revenue in New York City to exempt Ogawa from income tax on his official compensation prior to departure.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Regarding Masao Ogawa

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department acknowledges receipt of State's letter regarding the tax exemption of Yasumichi Tasaka.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (John W. Hanes)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John W. Hanes acknowledges receipt of State's letter of January 31, 1939, enclosing the Japanese Ambassador's note concerning Yasumichi Tasaka. Hanes reports that the matter is under immediate consideration in the Bureau of Internal Revenue and that State will be advised further at the earliest practicable date.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Yasumichi Tasaka

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State informs the Japanese Ambassador that Treasury has approved tax exemption for Tatsuo Shiraki.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State refers to Embassy Note No. 216 of December 8, 1938, regarding Tatsuo Shiraki of the Japanese Government Railways. The Ambassador is informed that Treasury holds Shiraki exempt from Federal income tax on his official compensation and that appropriate instructions will be issued to the Collector of Internal Revenue at the Customhouse in New York.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Regarding Tatsuo Shiraki

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms that Minoru Yagami was granted tax exemption and the New York Collector notified before his departure.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (John W. Hanes)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John W. Hanes writes regarding Minoru Yagami of the Japanese Government Railways. Pursuant to State's certification under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1938, Treasury holds Yagami's official compensation exempt from Federal income tax. Hanes notes that the Collector of Internal Revenue in New York was informed of Yagami's exempt status and departure date on January 26, 1939.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Minoru Yagami

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State informs the Japanese Ambassador of Treasury's formal confirmation of tax exemption for Minoru Yagami.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State refers to Japanese Note No. 8 of January 14, 1939, regarding the departure of Minoru Yagami on the Aquitania. The Ambassador is notified that Treasury held Yagami's official compensation exempt from Federal income tax and that the Collector of Internal Revenue in New York was informed accordingly on January 26, 1939.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Regarding Minoru Yagami

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests tax exemption for Yoshio Yeto, Manager of the Japan Association for the New York and San Francisco International Expositions.
subfiles.summary: In Note No. 27, the Japanese Ambassador requests that Yoshio Yeto be included in the list of tax-exempt Japanese officials. Yeto serves as Manager of the Japan Association for the New York and San Francisco International Expositions, with headquarters in the Consulate General of Japan in New York City. His salary is derived solely from the Japanese Government for official services rendered.
subfiles.title: Note No. 27 from the Japanese Embassy to the Secretary of State Regarding Yoshio Yeto

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State certifies Yoshio Yeto for income tax exemption under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1938.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits Embassy Note No. 27 regarding Yoshio Yeto to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr. Under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1938, Hull certifies that Japan grants reciprocal exemptions and that Yeto's services are similar to those of U.S. officers abroad. Hull expresses the hope that Yeto will be exempted from Federal income taxation and instructions issued to revenue authorities.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury Regarding Yoshio Yeto
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury (Henry Morgenthau, Jr.)

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges the tax exemption request for Yoshio Yeto and confirms transmission to Treasury.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Note No. 27 of February 15, 1939, regarding the desired income tax exemption for Yoshio Yeto. The Japanese Ambassador is informed that a copy has been transmitted to the competent authority of the United States Government to arrange for the exemption.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Regarding Yoshio Yeto

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests tax exemption and departure facilitation for language officer Sakae Yagi.
subfiles.summary: In Note No. 24, the Japanese Ambassador states that Sakae Yagi, a language officer of the Department of Education studying in the United States, will depart San Francisco on April 27, 1939, aboard the Kamakura Maru. As his salary was derived solely from the Japanese Government, the Embassy requests that steps be taken to exempt him from income taxes and facilitate his departure.
subfiles.title: Note No. 24 from the Japanese Embassy to the Secretary of State Regarding Sakae Yagi

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State certifies language officer Sakae Yagi for tax exemption under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1938.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull encloses Embassy Note No. 24 regarding Sakae Yagi in a letter to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr. Hull certifies under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1938 that Japan grants reciprocal exemptions to American personnel and that Yagi's duties are similar in character. He requests that appropriate instructions be issued to exempt Yagi from Federal income taxation prior to his departure.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury Regarding Sakae Yagi
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury (Henry Morgenthau, Jr.)

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges the tax exemption request for Sakae Yagi and reports transmission to Treasury.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Note No. 24 of February 14, 1939, concerning Sakae Yagi. The note informs the Japanese Ambassador that the request has been transmitted to the competent U.S. authority with a view to exempting Yagi from Federal income tax when he departs from San Francisco on April 27, 1939.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Regarding Sakae Yagi

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms the tax exemption of Masao Ogawa and notification of the New York Collector.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (John W. Hanes)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John W. Hanes writes regarding Masao Ogawa of the Japanese Financial Commission. In view of State's certification under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1938, Treasury holds Ogawa's official compensation exempt from Federal income tax. Hanes notes that the Collector of Internal Revenue at the Customhouse in New York was advised by telegram on February 2, 1939, of Ogawa's exempt status and intended sailing date.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Masao Ogawa

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State informs the Japanese Ambassador of the formal Treasury ruling exempting Masao Ogawa from income tax.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State refers to Note No. 17 of February 1, 1939, regarding Masao Ogawa. The Ambassador is informed that Treasury held Ogawa's compensation exempt under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1938, and that the Collector of Internal Revenue in New York was telegraphed on February 2, 1939, regarding his exempt status and departure.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Regarding Masao Ogawa

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department rules that Yasumichi Tasaka of the Japanese Government Railways is exempt from Federal income tax.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (John W. Hanes)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John W. Hanes references State's letter of January 31, 1939, regarding Yasumichi Tasaka. Based on State's certification under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1938, Treasury holds that Tasaka's official compensation is exempt from Federal income tax. The Collector of Internal Revenue in New York City will be advised accordingly.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Yasumichi Tasaka

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State informs the Japanese Ambassador that Yasumichi Tasaka has been granted income tax exemption.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State refers to Note No. 11 of January 24, 1939, regarding Yasumichi Tasaka. The Ambassador is notified that the Treasury Department holds Tasaka exempt from Federal income tax under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1938, and that the appropriate collector of internal revenue in New York City will be instructed accordingly.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Regarding Yasumichi Tasaka

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department acknowledges receipt of the request regarding tax exemption for Yoshio Yeto.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (John W. Hanes)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John W. Hanes acknowledges State's letter of February 23, 1939, concerning Yoshio Yeto of the Japan Association for the New York and San Francisco International Expositions. Hanes reports that the subject matter is receiving careful consideration and that State will be further advised at the earliest practicable date.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Yoshio Yeto

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department acknowledges receipt of the request regarding tax exemption for Sakae Yagi.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (John W. Hanes)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John W. Hanes acknowledges receipt of State's letter of February 24, 1939, enclosing the note concerning Sakae Yagi of the Japanese Department of Education. Hanes states that the matter is receiving careful consideration and further advice will follow as soon as practicable.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Sakae Yagi

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests tax exemption for Professor Shinichiro Kasugai during his study visit to the United States.
subfiles.summary: In Note No. 52, the Japanese Ambassador requests that Professor Shinichiro Kasugai of Tokyo Imperial University be granted exemption from income taxes. Kasugai was sent by the Department of Education to study in the United States for about one month, having arrived in New York on February 25, 1939, and scheduled to sail from San Francisco on March 30 aboard the Tatsuta Maru.
subfiles.title: Note No. 52 from the Japanese Embassy to the Secretary of State Regarding Shinichiro Kasugai

subfiles.about: The Acting Secretary of State certifies Professor Shinichiro Kasugai for tax exemption under Section 116(h).
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of State Sumner Welles transmits a copy of Embassy Note No. 52 concerning Professor Shinichiro Kasugai. In accordance with Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1938, Welles certifies reciprocal exemption by Japan and similarity of official service. He requests that Treasury instruct internal revenue authorities to grant Kasugai exemption prior to his scheduled departure from San Francisco on March 30.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury Regarding Shinichiro Kasugai
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury (Henry Morgenthau, Jr.)

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges the tax exemption request for Shinichiro Kasugai and reports transmission to Treasury.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Note No. 52 of March 14, 1939, concerning Shinichiro Kasugai. The note informs the Japanese Ambassador that a copy has been forwarded to the competent authority of the United States Government with a view to granting the exemption on his official compensation.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Regarding Shinichiro Kasugai

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests tax exemption for language officer Shuzo Takeda upon completion of his study tour.
subfiles.summary: In Note No. 53, the Japanese Ambassador requests that Shuzo Takeda, a language officer sent by the Department of Education to study in the United States for two months, be granted income tax exemption. Takeda arrived in New York from Germany on February 21, 1939, and is scheduled to depart San Francisco on March 30 aboard the Tatsuta Maru.
subfiles.title: Note No. 53 from the Japanese Embassy to the Secretary of State Regarding Shuzo Takeda

subfiles.about: The Acting Secretary of State certifies Shuzo Takeda for tax exemption under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1938.
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of State Sumner Welles transmits Japanese Note No. 53 regarding Shuzo Takeda. Under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1938, Welles certifies reciprocal tax treatment by Japan and similarity of service, requesting that Treasury instruct revenue officials to grant Takeda exemption from Federal income tax before his departure on March 30.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury Regarding Shuzo Takeda
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury (Henry Morgenthau, Jr.)

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges the tax exemption request for Shuzo Takeda and reports referral to competent authorities.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Note No. 53 of March 15, 1939, regarding the tax exemption of Shuzo Takeda. The Japanese Ambassador is informed that the note has been transmitted to the competent authority of the United States Government to effect the requested exemption.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Regarding Shuzo Takeda

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests tax exemption for Tatsuto Toki, architect supervising the Japanese pavilion at the Golden Gate International Exposition.
subfiles.summary: In Note No. 54, the Japanese Ambassador requests that Tatsuto Toki, an architect of Tokyo Imperial University engaged by the Japanese Government to supervise the construction of the Japanese building at the Golden Gate International Exposition in San Francisco, be granted income tax exemption. Toki arrived in San Francisco on October 12, 1938, and is scheduled to depart New York on March 28, 1939, aboard the Bremen.
subfiles.title: Note No. 54 from the Japanese Embassy to the Secretary of State Regarding Tatsuto Toki

subfiles.about: The Acting Secretary of State certifies Tatsuto Toki for income tax exemption under Section 116(h).
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of State Sumner Welles transmits Embassy Note No. 54 concerning Tatsuto Toki. Pursuant to Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1938, Welles certifies reciprocal exemption in Japan and similarity of official service. He requests that Treasury instruct appropriate revenue officials to exempt Toki from Federal income tax on his compensation before his departure from New York on March 28.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury Regarding Tatsuto Toki
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury (Henry Morgenthau, Jr.)

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges the request for tax exemption for Tatsuto Toki and reports transmission to Treasury.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Note No. 54 of March 16, 1939, regarding the tax exemption of architect Tatsuto Toki. The note informs the Japanese Ambassador that a copy has been forwarded to the competent authority of the United States Government to arrange for the exemption prior to Toki's departure on the Bremen.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Regarding Tatsuto Toki

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests tax exemption for Professor Hidetoshi Isobe during his official study visit to the United States.
subfiles.summary: In Note No. 56, the Japanese Ambassador requests that Professor Hidetoshi Isobe of Utsunomiya Agricultural College be included in the list of tax-exempt Japanese officials. Isobe was sent by the Department of Education to study in the United States for two months, having arrived in New York on February 13, 1939, and scheduled to depart San Francisco on April 27 aboard the Kamakura Maru.
subfiles.title: Note No. 56 from the Japanese Embassy to the Secretary of State Regarding Hidetoshi Isobe

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of the tax exemption request for Hidetoshi Isobe.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges Note No. 56 of March 14, 1939, regarding Hidetoshi Isobe. The Japanese Ambassador is advised that the note has been transmitted to the competent authority of the United States Government with a view to exempting Isobe from Federal income taxation on his official compensation.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Regarding Hidetoshi Isobe

subfiles.about: The Acting Secretary of State certifies Professor Hidetoshi Isobe for tax exemption under Section 116(h).
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of State Sumner Welles transmits a copy of Japanese Embassy Note No. 56 concerning Professor Hidetoshi Isobe of Utsunomiya Agricultural College. Welles certifies under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1938 that Japan grants reciprocal exemptions and that Isobe's services are similar to those of American officials abroad, asking Treasury to instruct the appropriate authorities accordingly.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury Regarding Hidetoshi Isobe
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury (Henry Morgenthau, Jr.)

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests tax exemption and sailing facilitation for Assistant Professor Kazuo Tanaka and his wife Sumiko Tanaka.
subfiles.summary: In Note No. 57, the Japanese Ambassador requests that Kazuo Tanaka, Assistant Professor of Kyushu Imperial University traveling as a temporary visitor with his wife Mrs. Sumiko Tanaka, be granted income tax exemption. Tanaka arrived in New York on February 25, 1939, and plans to depart San Francisco on April 27 aboard the Kamakura Maru. The Embassy requests that appropriate authorities facilitate their departure.
subfiles.title: Note No. 57 from the Japanese Embassy to the Secretary of State Regarding Kazuo Tanaka and Wife

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State advises on sailing permit procedures for Kazuo Tanaka and wife in San Francisco.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges Note No. 57 of March 16, 1939, regarding the departure of Assistant Professor Kazuo Tanaka and his wife. The note advises that informal inquiry with the Bureau of Internal Revenue indicates Tanaka should visit the Revenue Agent in Charge, Room 225 Federal Office Building, Civic Center, San Francisco, prior to sailing, where presentation of his passport will secure a sailing permit.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Regarding Departure Procedures for Kazuo Tanaka

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests tax exemption for language officer Takeo Watanabe prior to his departure.
subfiles.summary: In Note No. 66, the Japanese Ambassador requests that Takeo Watanabe, a language officer of the Department of Education in Tokyo studying in the United States, be granted income tax exemption. Watanabe arrived in Boston on December 18, 1938, and is scheduled to leave San Francisco on April 27, 1939, aboard the Kamakura Maru. The Embassy asks that U.S. authorities be notified to facilitate his departure.
subfiles.title: Note No. 66 from the Japanese Embassy to the Secretary of State Regarding Takeo Watanabe

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State certifies Takeo Watanabe for tax exemption under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits Embassy Note No. 66 regarding Takeo Watanabe of the Japanese Department of Education. Hull certifies under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code that Japan grants equivalent exemptions to U.S. government employees in Japan and that Watanabe's services are similar. He requests that Treasury instruct appropriate authorities to exempt Watanabe from income tax prior to his departure on April 27.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury Regarding Takeo Watanabe
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury (Henry Morgenthau, Jr.)

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges the tax exemption request for Takeo Watanabe and reports transmission to Treasury.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Note No. 66 of March 27, 1939, regarding Takeo Watanabe's desired income tax exemption. The note informs the Japanese Ambassador that a copy has been transmitted to the competent authority of the United States Government to effect the tax exemption on his official compensation.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Regarding Takeo Watanabe

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms that Yoshio Yeto is exempt from Federal income tax.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (Stephen B. Gibbons)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury Stephen B. Gibbons references State's letter of February 23, 1939, regarding Yoshio Yeto, Manager of the Japan Association for the New York and San Francisco International Expositions. In view of State's certification under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1938, Treasury holds Yeto's compensation exempt from Federal income tax. Appropriate instructions will be issued to collectors of internal revenue in New York City.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Yoshio Yeto

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State notifies the Japanese Ambassador that Yoshio Yeto has been granted income tax exemption.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State refers to Japanese Note No. 27 of February 15, 1939, regarding Yoshio Yeto. The Ambassador is advised that Treasury holds Yeto's official compensation exempt from Federal income tax based on State's certification, and that appropriate instructions will be issued to the Collectors of Internal Revenue in New York City.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Regarding Yoshio Yeto

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department rules that language officer Sakae Yagi is exempt from Federal income tax.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (Stephen B. Gibbons)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury Stephen B. Gibbons writes regarding Sakae Yagi, language officer of the Japanese Department of Education. Based on the State Department's certification under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1938, Treasury holds Yagi's compensation exempt from Federal income tax. Appropriate instructions will be issued to the Collector of Internal Revenue in San Francisco, California.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Sakae Yagi

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State informs the Japanese Ambassador of the tax exemption granted to Sakae Yagi prior to sailing.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State refers to Note No. 24 of February 14, 1939, regarding Sakae Yagi. The Ambassador is informed that Treasury holds Yagi exempt from Federal income tax on his official compensation and that instructions will be issued to the Collector of Internal Revenue in San Francisco, from which port Yagi is scheduled to sail on April 27 aboard the Kamakura Maru.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Regarding Sakae Yagi

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department acknowledges receipt of the request regarding tax exemption for Shinichiro Kasugai.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (John W. Hanes)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John W. Hanes acknowledges receipt of State's letter of March 21, 1939, concerning Shinichiro Kasugai's desired income tax exemption. Hanes notes that the matter is receiving careful consideration and that State will be promptly advised at the earliest practicable date.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Shinichiro Kasugai

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department acknowledges receipt of the request regarding tax exemption for Shuzo Takeda.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (John W. Hanes)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John W. Hanes acknowledges State's letter of March 21, 1939, regarding the tax exemption of language officer Shuzo Takeda. Hanes reports that the matter is receiving careful consideration by the Treasury Department and advice will follow promptly.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Shuzo Takeda

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests tax exemption and departure facilitation for Commander Ko Nagasawa.
subfiles.summary: In Note No. 74, the Japanese Ambassador requests that Commander Ko Nagasawa, a language officer sent to the United States in May 1937 by the Navy Department of Japan to study, be included in the list of tax-exempt officials. Nagasawa's income is derived solely from the Japanese Government, and he is scheduled to sail from Los Angeles on April 24, 1939, aboard the Kamakura Maru.
subfiles.title: Note No. 74 from the Japanese Embassy to the Secretary of State Regarding Commander Ko Nagasawa

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State certifies Commander Ko Nagasawa for tax exemption under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull encloses Japanese Embassy Note No. 74 concerning Commander Ko Nagasawa. Under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, Hull certifies reciprocal exemption in Japan and similarity of official service. He requests that Treasury instruct appropriate revenue officials to exempt Commander Nagasawa prior to his departure from Los Angeles on April 24.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury Regarding Commander Ko Nagasawa
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury (Henry Morgenthau, Jr.)

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges the tax exemption request for Commander Ko Nagasawa and reports transmission to Treasury.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Note No. 74 of April 7, 1939, concerning the departure and requested tax exemption of Commander Ko Nagasawa. The Ambassador is informed that the note has been transmitted to the competent authority of the United States Government to facilitate Nagasawa's tax exemption.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Regarding Commander Ko Nagasawa

subfiles.about: Internal State Department inquiry regarding the official recognition and notification of the Formosan Government Commissioner in New York.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs (Joseph W. Ballantine)
subfiles.summary: Joseph W. Ballantine of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs refers to an attached letter to the Treasury Department concerning tax exemption for Japanese officials. Ballantine notes that the Japanese Ambassador's list includes the Formosan Government Commissioner at New York City (Shuhei Kawazoe), an office of which the U.S. Government does not appear to have been officially notified. He asks whether there is any objection to forwarding the letter to the Treasury Department.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum on the Status of the Formosan Government Commissioner at New York
subfiles.to: Co (Division of Commercial Policy and Agreements / Legal Adviser)

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador submits a comprehensive roster of Japanese non-diplomatic officials stationed in the United States for tax exemption.
subfiles.summary: In Note No. 76, dated April 14, 1939, the Japanese Ambassador transmits a detailed list of Japanese nationals resident in the United States (other than diplomatic and consular officers) receiving official compensation, in order to facilitate their income tax exemption. The attached four-page schedule lists 36 officials across various bodies, including the Formosan Government Commissioner, Imperial Japanese Army Inspectors' Office, Japanese Government Raw Silk Intelligence Bureau, Japanese Government Railways, Imperial Japanese Navy Inspector's Office, Financial Commission, Tokyo Commercial and Industrial Museum, and visiting academic researchers and language officers.
subfiles.title: Note No. 76 from the Japanese Embassy to the Secretary of State Transmitting Comprehensive List of Non-Diplomatic Officials

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of the roster of Japanese officials and requests domestic addresses for visiting scholars.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges Note No. 76 of April 14, 1939, and its enclosed roster of Japanese officials. The Ambassador is informed that the note and list have been transmitted to the competent U.S. authorities with a view to granting tax exemptions. The Secretary further requests that the Embassy provide United States addresses for the individual scholars and officers listed in the final section so internal revenue authorities can be instructed.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Acknowledging Note No. 76 and Requesting Addresses

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State certifies the comprehensive list of Japanese non-diplomatic officials for tax exemption under Section 116(h).
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits a copy of Embassy Note No. 76 and its enclosed roster of non-diplomatic Japanese officials in the United States. Hull cites prior statutory precedents and Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, certifying reciprocity and similarity of functions. He requests that Treasury instruct appropriate revenue authorities to grant income tax exemptions, noting that the Japanese Ambassador has been asked to furnish domestic addresses for the scholars listed in the final section.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury Transmitting Roster of Japanese Officials
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury (Henry Morgenthau, Jr.)

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department rules that language officer Shuzo Takeda is exempt from Federal income tax.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (John W. Hanes)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John W. Hanes replies to State's letter of March 21, 1939, regarding language officer Shuzo Takeda. In view of State's certification under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1938, Treasury holds Takeda's official compensation exempt from Federal income tax. Appropriate instructions have been issued to the Collector of Internal Revenue and the Internal Revenue Agent in Charge in San Francisco, California.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Shuzo Takeda

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department acknowledges receipt of the request regarding tax exemption for Takeo Watanabe.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (John W. Hanes)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John W. Hanes acknowledges receipt of State's letter of April 1, 1939, enclosing Embassy Note No. 66 concerning language officer Takeo Watanabe. Hanes states that the matter is receiving careful consideration and that State will be promptly advised at the earliest practicable date.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Takeo Watanabe
